focus.jtag: Iran signals readiness for a more intense war; Brent tops $101 (first since May), yields near 3-yr highs into PPI/CPI and Oracle's AI-signaling print
focus.jnote: The tape stays under an oil-and-war cloud, now stacked on a data gauntlet. Brent crude climbed above $101 — a fresh high since May — after Iran said it is ready for a more intense conflict and vowed to resist the U.S. naval blockade. WTI rose above $97. Equity futures are little changed — S&P futures roughly flat with Nasdaq contracts slipping ~0.4% — as investors await inflation data and Oracle’s results, seen as a test of tolerance for AI-spending risk. The oil bid keeps the 10-year yield near three-year highs (~4.85%). PPI hits at 8:30 ET today and August CPI lands tomorrow, with the FOMC 9/15–16. A live, open-ended conflict stacked on PPI/CPI and an FOMC is not a premium-selling setup.
focus.notdown: Energy (XLE, XOM, MPC, OXY) and Defense (LMT, RTX, NOC, and small-caps like AVAV) keep the fundamental bid — oil supply fear lifts energy, conflict-demand lifts defense. But these are two-sided war trades, not clean Snipers: any credible Hormuz-easing or de-escalation headline gaps energy straight back down (recall March, when Brent fell ~9% in a session on de-escalation signals). Watch-only, and note the shipping/defense names the scanner boarded are all flagged thinly traded.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive growth and fuel-sensitive transports (airlines) are the pressured groups — higher oil and a ~4.85% 10-year weigh on both. But selling bear calls into a VIX ticking up off its lows, with PPI today, CPI tomorrow, and an FOMC next week that can reprice the curve either way, is exactly the blow-up 4-VAL exists to prevent. The disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite 62 is squarely WARM and P(≥1% gap) at 42% is above the 35% trigger — either one alone locks out GREEN. Layer on a live U.S.–Iran military exchange with Brent above $101, plus PPI (today), CPI (Fri 9/11) and the FOMC (9/15–16) all inside a normal DTE, and the overnight tail is skewed and hard to size. The four boarded names are all flagged illiquid / OI-thin / liquidity-unverified. Stand down on new credit spreads, or if you must be positioned, use 7-DTE that clears CPI and the FOMC and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

Oracle tonight; single-stock landmines — Oracle’s results are a read on AI-spending tolerance and can swing megacap tech and the boarded names are all thinly traded. Keep every spread clear of its name’s catalyst and confirm liquidity.

With Brent above $101 feeding inflation fear and yields near 4.85%, keep every spread clear of both inflation prints and the FOMC window.
